sheets.what: The names left off each state's draft roll, with the reasons each Chief Electoral Officer gave
sheets.cannot: Reasons are what the officers wrote down, and nobody checked them. Some states printed their figures in lakh, and the figures column says which.
columns: The state or union territory, one row for each of the 32 in the revision.
The phase of the revision the state was in, where 1 is Bihar (order of 24 June 2025), 2 the states of the order of 27 October 2025 and 3 the states of the order of 14 May 2026.
The date the state's draft roll was published, as YYYY-MM-DD.
Electors on the roll before the revision as the Chief Electoral Officer gave it at the draft, as a count.
Names left off the draft roll, as a count, from the Chief Electoral Officer's figures (Bihar's from the phase 1 lists of names left off).
Names left off the draft per 100 electors on the roll before the revision.
Names left off the draft that were entered as dead, as a count, where the reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
Names left off the draft that were entered as shifted, absent or untraceable, or under any other reason the state reported, as a count.
Names left off the draft that were entered as enrolled more than once, as a count.
Names left off the draft that the published reasons do not account for, as a count, which is every name left off where no split by reason was published.

How far the reasons were published, where complete means the three add up to the names left off within rounding, short means they fall short of it, none means no split was published and pending means there is no draft yet.
Whether the state's figures are exact counts or were printed rounded, in lakh or crore.
Where the figures come from, where primary is a document of the Election Commission or a Chief Electoral Officer, press is a newspaper or broadcaster and lists is Bihar's own lists of names left off.
The address of the document the figures come from.
The date the final roll was published, as YYYY-MM-DD, blank where none has been found.
Names added between the draft and the final roll, as a count, blank where the state published only the net change.
Names deleted between the draft and the final roll, as a count.
Names kept off the final roll while their cases were adjudicated, as a count, which only West Bengal reported.
Electors on the final roll, as a count.
The final roll less the draft roll, a net change that counts new voters added after the draft as well as names put back.
Names left off the draft less net_after_draft, which is the net fall in the roll from before the revision to the final roll, as a count.
The net fall per 100 electors on the roll before the revision.
net_after_draft as a percentage of the names left off the draft, an upper bound on the share put back because the rise counts new voters too.
A plain note on how the state's draft figures were read or combined.
Electors on the roll before the revision per 100 people aged 18 and over projected for 1 March 2026 by the Technical Group on Population Projections.
Electors on the draft roll per 100 people aged 18 and over projected for 1 March 2026.
Names left off the draft as a percentage of the votes polled in the state at the 2024 Lok Sabha election.
Women as a percentage of the names left off the draft, where the state's split by sex is known.
Women as a percentage of the roll before the revision, where known.

How firm the split by sex is, where lists means counted from Bihar's lists, exact and rounded mean an official figure printed in full or rounded, proxy means the roll before is a stand-in roll and unverified means a press figure with no primary source.
Net state domestic product per head at current prices for 2023-24, in rupees, from the Reserve Bank's handbook of state statistics (MoSPI for Gujarat).
Average monthly spending per person in rural areas in 2023-24, in rupees, from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey without the value of free items.
Average monthly spending per person in urban areas in 2023-24, in rupees, from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey without the value of free items.
The urban share of the population projected for 1 March 2026 by the Technical Group, as a percentage.
The literacy rate of people aged 7 and over, as a percentage, from the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2023-24.
The literacy rate of women and girls aged 7 and over, as a percentage, from the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2023-24.
The share of households whose head is Muslim, as a percentage, from the National Family Health Survey 2019-21.
The share of households whose head is from a Scheduled Caste, as a percentage, from the National Family Health Survey 2019-21.
The share of households whose head is from a Scheduled Tribe, as a percentage, from the National Family Health Survey 2019-21.
Females per 1,000 males in the whole population, from the National Family Health Survey 2019-21.

People born in the state and counted in another Indian state at the 2011 census, as a percentage of the state's own population counted in 2011, from Census table D-01 (place of birth). For Bihar that is 79,49,853 over 10,40,99,452, or 7.64.

People counted in the state at the 2011 census who were born in another Indian state, as a percentage of the state's own population counted in 2011, from Census table D-01 (place of birth). People born outside India are not counted. For Bihar that is 10,66,526 over 10,40,99,452, or 1.02.
Whether the state has an international land border, yes or no, from the Ministry of Home Affairs.

sheets.what: Electors in every Lok Sabha election since 1984-85, with the population of voting age
sheets.cannot: The population counts residents who are not citizens.
columns: The Lok Sabha general election, by year (1984-85 includes Assam and Punjab, which polled in 1985).
Electors on the roll for that election across India, as a count, from the Election Commission's Atlas 2024, Graph 6.1.
The same electors in crore (ten million), to two decimal places.
The voting age at that election, 21 for 1984-85 and 18 from 1989 after the 61st Amendment.
India's population at or above the voting age on 1 July of the election year, as a count, from the UN World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant.
The same population of voting age in crore, to two decimal places.

Electors per 100 people of voting age, which can pass 100 if the population estimate is right and the roll holds names of the dead or moved, and which counts residents who are not citizens in the population.
A note on the row, such as the misprint corrected in the Atlas's 1991-92 figure.
The source of the electors figure, the Election Commission's Atlas 2024, Graph 6.1 (printed page 19).
The source of the population figure, the UN World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant, single-year ages, 1 July of the election year.

sheets.sheet: Names left off against 2024 Lok Sabha margins
sheets.what: The names left off each Lok Sabha seat against its 2024 winning margin
sheets.cannot: A count larger than the margin could have decided a seat. It does not show that it did.
columns: The state, one of the four with constituency figures (Bihar, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Kerala).
The Lok Sabha constituency number within the state.
The count named in what_is_counted, summed over the seat's assembly segments, using the segment list of the Election Commission's statistical report 34.

What count is used, which is the names left off or deleted in both phases in Bihar, the names left off the draft in Tamil Nadu, and the fall in the roll up to the 2026 election in West Bengal (from the 2024 roll) and Kerala (from the January 2025 roll), a change that takes in ordinary additions and deletions as well as the revision.
The seat's winning margin in votes at the 2024 Lok Sabha election.
The party that won the seat in 2024, as the results print it.
The party that came second in 2024, as the results print it.
Whether count is larger than margin_2024, yes or no, which says the count was large enough to decide the seat and says nothing about whether it did.
The source of the 2024 results and segments, the Election Commission's results and statistical report 34 through a published compilation of them.

sheets.what: Each final roll set against the draft, with names added and deleted after it
sheets.cannot: Several states gave only the net rise from draft to final. The rise counts new voters too, so it is the most that could have been restored.
columns: The state or union territory, listed where a final roll or its date has been found.
The phase of the revision the state was in, 1, 2 or 3.
Electors on the roll before the revision, as a count, from the state table.
Names left off the draft roll, as a count.
The date the final roll was published, as YYYY-MM-DD.
Names added between the draft and the final roll, as a count, blank where the state published only the net change.
Names deleted between the draft and the final roll, as a count, blank where none was published.
Names kept off the final roll while their cases were adjudicated, as a count (West Bengal only).
Electors on the final roll, as a count.
The final roll less the draft roll in the final-roll source, a net change that counts new voters added after the draft as well as names put back.
Names left off the draft less final_less_draft, which is the net fall in the roll from before the revision to the final roll, as a count.
The net fall per 100 electors on the roll before the revision.

Whether draft plus added less deleted and withheld equals the final roll, where exact means to the elector, rounded means within rounding, net only means the state gave the net rise in place of the gross figures, and no means the published figures do not add up.
The address of the document the final-roll figures come from.

sheets.what: Women's share of the names left off against their share of the roll
sheets.cannot: Only states that published a split by sex. Each row carries its quality flag.
columns: The state or union territory, listed where the names left off the draft have been found split by sex.
The phase of the revision the state was in, 1, 2 or 3.
Women among the names left off the draft, as a count (Bihar's counted from the phase 1 lists of names left off).
Men among the names left off the draft, as a count.
Women as a percentage of the women and men left off the draft.
Women as a percentage of the roll before the revision.
women_pct_of_removed less women_pct_of_roll, in percentage points.

How firm the split by sex is, where lists means counted from Bihar's lists, exact and rounded mean an official figure printed in full or rounded, proxy means the roll before is a stand-in roll and unverified means a press figure with no primary source.
A plain note on where the split by sex comes from and how it was read.
The address of the source of the split by sex, blank for Bihar, whose figures are counted from the lists.

sheets.what: Every order, letter, court order and judgment that changed how the revision was run
sheets.cannot: Primary documents only. Press reports are on the process page, apart.
columns: The date of the order, letter, judgment or release, as YYYY-MM-DD.
Who issued it, the Election Commission, the Supreme Court or a state election officer.
Which part of the revision the entry concerns (Bihar, Phase II, Phase III, West Bengal or Assam).
A short title for the change.
A plain account of what the document changed in the rules or dates of the revision.
The names of the documents the entry rests on, separated by a vertical bar.
The addresses of those documents, in the same order, separated by a vertical bar.

sheets.what: Each state's schedule as set and as moved
columns: The state or union territory the schedule is for.
The phase of the revision the state was in, written I, II or III.
The order, letter or release the dates come from, or a label saying the dates are those the state actually published.
Whether the dates are those the state actually kept as published (yes) or dates that were set in advance (no).
The first day of enumeration, the house-to-house round of forms, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The last day of enumeration, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The date of the draft roll, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The first day for claims and objections against the draft, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The last day for claims and objections, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The first day of the period for notices and hearings, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The last day of the period for notices and hearings, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The date of the final roll, as YYYY-MM-DD.
The address of the document the dates come from.

sheets.what: Electors kept on a draft roll but sent a notice, by state
sheets.cannot: Most figures are running counts reported by the press. The two lists overlap, so they can add up to more than the total.
columns: The phase of the revision the state was in, 1, 2 or 3.
Electors on the draft roll, worked out as the roll before the revision less the names left off, as a count.
Electors kept on the draft roll but sent a notice to prove their entry, as a count. Where sources differ, one published total is used for each state.
How the notices total was got, where published means a total the source printed and sum means the two lists added because the source gave no total.
Notices per 100 electors on the draft roll.
Whether the notices figure is primary (a document of the Election Commission or a Chief Electoral Officer) or press (a newspaper or broadcaster).
Whether the notices figure was printed rounded, True or False.
The date of the source for the notices figure, as YYYY-MM-DD, and many later figures are running counts taken while notices were still being heard.
Electors sent a notice because they could not be linked to the roll of the last intensive revision, as a count, where published.
Electors sent a notice from the Commission's logical discrepancy list of mismatched names, ages and family links, as a count, where published, and an elector can be on both lists.
Names deleted after a notice, as a count, the latest figure found.
The address of the source of the notices figure.
The address of the source of the two list figures.

sheets.what: Large cities set against their suburbs and the rest of their state
sheets.cannot: A city is a set of districts, drawn differently from city to city. Kolkata and Kochi are measured by the fall in the roll.
columns: The city, drawn as the districts named in districts.
The state the row's districts are in, which for Delhi's ring is Uttar Pradesh.

What is counted, where left_off means names left off the draft and fall means the fall in the roll from an earlier roll to the draft (West Bengal from the 2024 Lok Sabha roll, Kerala from the January 2025 roll), a change that takes in ordinary deaths and moves as well.
Which part of the city the row covers, where core is the city's own districts, ring the neighbouring districts and rest the rest of the state.
The districts the row adds up, separated by a semicolon character, or rest of state.
Electors on the roll the count is measured against, the roll named in base_roll_is.
Which roll base_roll is. It is the roll before the revision everywhere except Patna (the 2025 election roll), Kolkata (the 2024 Lok Sabha roll) and Kochi (the January 2025 roll).
Names left off the draft, or for Kolkata and Kochi the fall in the roll to the draft, as a count (Patna counts both of Bihar's phases).
The same rate for the city's whole state.
A note where the row's figures differ in kind, marking Hyderabad's figures as reported in the press and Patna's as per 100 on the 2025 roll.

sheets.what: Seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes against general seats
sheets.cannot: A reserved seat describes a place. It says nothing about the caste of the electors left off.
columns: The count and its base, which is names left off or deleted in both phases per 100 on the 2025 roll for Bihar, names left off per 100 on the roll before for Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Delhi, and the fall in the roll to the draft per 100 for West Bengal (from the 2024 roll) and Kerala (from the January 2025 roll).
The kind of seat under the Delimitation Order of 2008, GEN for general, SC for Scheduled Castes and ST for Scheduled Tribes.
The number of assembly seats in that category.
The count per 100 electors across all seats in the category, in the measure named.
The average, over the reserved seats, of each seat's rate less the rate of the general seats in its own district, in points per 100, blank for general seats.
How many reserved seats have a higher rate than the general seats of their own district.
How many reserved seats had general seats in their district to be compared with.

sheets.what: Districts on the international border against the interior
sheets.cannot: The rate says nothing about citizenship.
columns: The count and its base, which is names left off per 100 on the roll before (Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat), names left off or deleted in both phases per 100 on the 2025 roll (Bihar), the fall in the roll per 100 from the 2024 roll to the draft (West Bengal) and names deleted after the draft per 1,000 on the draft (Uttarakhand).

Which districts the row covers, where border is every district on the Government of India's list of Border Guarding Districts, interior the rest, interior_without_city the rest without the city's districts, and border district names one listed district.
The number of districts in the row.
Electors on the roll the measure divides by, summed over the districts, blank on single-district rows.
The count the measure names, summed over the districts, blank on single-district rows.
count per 100 electors on base, or per 1,000 for Uttarakhand.
The share of the count entered as dead, as a percentage, where reasons were published (Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat), and the reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
The share of the count entered as shifted or absent, as a percentage, where reasons were published.
The share of the count entered as enrolled somewhere else, as a percentage, where reasons were published.

sheets.sheet: Women, state by state and district by district
sheets.what: Every count by sex the site holds, state and district
sheets.cannot: Each state is measured in its own way, named in the measure column. Rows from different measures are not comparable.
columns: Whether the row is a whole state or one district.
The district, blank on state rows.

The count the row's shares are of. For district rows it names the state's own measure, such as the names left off or deleted in both phases in Bihar or the fall from the 2024 roll to the 2026 election roll in West Bengal.

Women as a percentage of the roll the count is taken from (the roll before for states, Bihar's draft plus phase 1 names left off the draft, the 2024 and January 2025 rolls for West Bengal and Kerala, and the draft for Uttarakhand).
Women as a percentage of the count named in measure.
women_share_of_count less women_share_of_roll, in percentage points.
Women left off the draft per 100 women on the roll before, where the roll by sex is the roll before times women's share of it, on state rows only.
Men left off the draft per 100 men on the roll before, on state rows only.
How firm the state's split by sex is (lists, exact, rounded, proxy or unverified), on state rows only.
The address of the source of the state's split by sex, on state rows only.

sheets.what: Rural, mixed and urban districts inside each state
sheets.cannot: Urban shares are from the 2011 census. Each state is measured in its own way.
columns: What is counted, where left_off means names left off the draft per 100 on the roll before, roll_2025 means Bihar's names left off or deleted in both phases per 100 on the 2025 roll, and fall means the fall in the roll to the draft (West Bengal from the 2024 roll, Kerala from the January 2025 roll).
The district as it stood at the 2011 census, which is the unit each row adds up.
The 2011 census code of that district.
The present districts counted under it, each under the 2011 district it was mostly made from, separated by a semicolon character.
The share of the 2011 district's people living in towns at the 2011 census, as a percentage, from table A-01.
rural where urban_pct_2011 is under 20, mixed from 20 to 50, and urban above 50.
Electors on the roll the count is measured against, summed over the districts, as a count.
Names left off, or the fall in the roll, summed over the districts, as a count.

sheets.what: District circumstances from NFHS-5 beside the rate, inside each state
sheets.cannot: Survey figures are for 2019-21, from a published compilation of the district fact sheets. Each state is measured in its own way.
columns: What is counted, where left_off means names left off the draft per 100 on the roll before, roll_2025 means Bihar's names left off or deleted in both phases per 100 on the 2025 roll, and fall means the fall in the roll to the draft (West Bengal from the 2024 roll, Kerala from the January 2025 roll), change_2023 means Rajasthan's fall in the roll from the 2023 election roll to the final roll of 2026 per 100, and after_draft means Uttarakhand's names deleted after the draft per 100 on the draft.
The district as the National Family Health Survey 2019-21 published it, which is the unit each row adds up. Delhi's are the 11 districts of its 2025 roll.
The present districts counted under it, separated by a semicolon character. A district made after the survey is counted under the one it was made from.
Electors on the roll the count is measured against, summed over the districts, as a count.
Names left off, or the fall in the roll, summed over the districts, as a count.
Women aged 15 to 49 who can read, as a percentage, NFHS-5 district fact sheet indicator 14.
Women aged 15 to 49 with ten or more years of schooling, as a percentage, NFHS-5 indicator 15.
Women aged 20 to 24 married before age 18, as a percentage, NFHS-5 indicator 16.
Households using clean fuel for cooking, as a percentage, NFHS-5 indicator 10.
Population living in households that use an improved sanitation facility, as a percentage, NFHS-5 indicator 9.
Deaths in the three years before the survey that were registered with the civil authority, as a percentage, NFHS-5 indicator 6.
Females per 1,000 males in the whole population, NFHS-5 indicator 3.

sheets.what: Every court case, resolution, protest, Form 7 dispute and software change on the disputes page, with its source
sheets.cannot: Press items are what the outlet reported. Allegations are the party's. Nothing here says what anyone intended.
columns: The section of the disputes page the item sits in, such as the courts, Form 7 objections or changes to the software.
The date of the order, resolution or report, as the source gives it.
The state or union territory the item concerns, or India for the revision as a whole.
Constituencies, districts or cities the item names, separated by semicolons. Blank where it names none.
The court, magistrate or tribunal, where the item is a case or an order. Blank otherwise.
The parties, officials' offices and organisations that act in the item, separated by semicolons. No private person is named.
One to three issues the item concerns, from a fixed list, separated by semicolons.
Document when the item quotes the court, the Assembly or the Commission itself, report when it quotes a named press report.
The court, body or outlet the item comes from.
One sentence saying what the source records or reports, attributed to it.
The Commission's or the official's reply as the same source reported it, where there was one.

sheets.what: Every application under the Right to Information Act about the revision whose reply was published or reported, with what was asked and what came back
sheets.cannot: A list of the applications that were reported. No authority publishes how many were filed. Each answer is what the outlet reported.
columns: The state the application concerns, or All India for one about the revision as a whole.
The public authority the application went to, such as the Election Commission or a state's Chief Electoral Officer.
The organisation that filed it, or the applicant's role. No private person is named.
The date the application was filed, where it was reported.
The date of the reply, where it was reported.
Days from the application to the reply, where both dates were reported. The Act allows 30.
What became of it: no record held, refused, transferred, partly supplied, supplied, appeal, no reply in time or pending.
What the authority said or did, as reported.
The section of the Act cited for a refusal, if any.
primary if the reply itself was read, press if the item rests on a report.
The outlet that published the reply or reported it.

sheets.sheet: Every constituency in four states, the roll through the revision
sheets.what: Every constituency of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal and Uttarakhand in one table
sheets.cannot: Each state measures a different thing, named in the state's rows. Nothing is added across states. Only Uttarakhand has gross additions and deletions.
columns: The state, one of the four that published their rolls by constituency (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal and Uttarakhand).
The district the constituency lies in.

The earliest roll in the row, which is the roll of 27 October 2025 worked out as the draft plus the names left off for Tamil Nadu, the January 2025 final roll for Kerala, the 2024 Lok Sabha roll for West Bengal and blank for Uttarakhand.
Names left off the draft, as a count, given by constituency only in Tamil Nadu.
Electors on the draft roll (19 December 2025 in Tamil Nadu, 23 December 2025 in Kerala, 16 December 2025 in West Bengal, July 2026 in Uttarakhand).
Claims admitted after the draft, as a count, Uttarakhand only, from the Chief Electoral Officer's PN 63/2026.
Objections admitted after the draft, as a count, Uttarakhand only, from PN 63/2026.
The latest roll in the row, the final roll of 23 February 2026 in Tamil Nadu, 21 February 2026 in Kerala and 3 October 2026 in Uttarakhand, and the roll at the 2026 nominations in West Bengal.
later_roll less draft, a net change that counts new voters added after the draft as well as names put back.
later_roll less earlier_roll, as a count, which is negative where the roll fell.

sheets.what: Every Bihar constituency, with names left off or deleted by phase, reason and sex, and the 2020 to 2025 results
sheets.cannot: Religion is guessed from names and given as a range. Reasons are what the officers wrote down.
columns: The assembly constituency number in Bihar, from 1 to 243.
The assembly constituency's name as Wikipedia's list of Bihar's assembly constituencies spells it.
The district the constituency lies in, as Wikipedia's list of Bihar's assembly constituencies gives it.
The Lok Sabha seat the constituency is a segment of, from Wikipedia's list, with Minapur (90) placed in Vaishali as the 2008 delimitation has it.
Whether the seat is reserved, written SC for Scheduled Castes, ST for Scheduled Tribes and GEN for a general seat, from Wikipedia's list.
The border the constituency lies on (Nepal, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand or West Bengal, with two joined by a semicolon character) or Interior where it lies on none.
Electors in the constituency at the November 2025 election, from the Election Commission's Detailed Results, 7,46,91,135 in all. It is the base every Bihar rate per 100 electors divides by.
The number of polling booths in the constituency in the booth-level count of names left off, set on the 2024 Lok Sabha Form 20 results.

Names left off the draft in phase 1, the round that produced the draft roll of 1 August 2025, as a count from the Chief Electoral Officer's table of what it calls deletions by constituency, phase and sex.

Names deleted after the draft in phase 2, from the Chief Electoral Officer's table, with no reason recorded. They come to 3,51,150, below the 3,66,742 deleted after the draft in the Commission's Format 4B return in every one of the 243 seats, by 4 to 586 names, while tracking it almost exactly seat by seat. That is the pattern of an earlier count of the same deletions. Neither table is dated.
Names left off or deleted in both phases together (p1 plus p2), as a count from the Chief Electoral Officer's table.
Names left off or deleted in both phases per 100 electors, with electorate_2025 as the base.
Women among the names left off or deleted in both phases, as a count from the Chief Electoral Officer's table by sex.
Men among the names left off or deleted in both phases, as a count from the Chief Electoral Officer's table by sex.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as dead, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off, where the reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as shifted, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as absent, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as already enrolled somewhere else, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off.
Phase 1 names left off the draft whose names were guessed from names to be Hindu, summed from the booth-level file of names left off by sex and religion, since the roll itself records no religion.
Phase 1 names left off the draft whose names were guessed from names to be Muslim, summed from the same booth-level file.
Phase 1 names left off the draft whose names could not be guessed as either Hindu or Muslim, summed from the same booth-level file.
The party that won the seat at the 2020 Bihar assembly election, with party spellings made uniform.
The 2020 winner's alliance as the alliances stood in 2020, where NDA is BJP, JD(U), VIP and HAM(S), INDIA is RJD, INC and the Left parties, and Other is every other party including LJP.
The 2020 winning margin in votes, the winner's votes less the runner-up's, from the Election Commission's Detailed Results for 2020.

The party with the most votes in the constituency's segment at the 2024 Lok Sabha election, summed from booth-level Form 20 results for the top three parties in each booth, with the party labels corrected in nine Lok Sabha seats.
The alliance of the seg2024 party at the 2024 election, written NDA, INDIA or Other.
The party that won the seat at the 2025 Bihar assembly election, from Wikipedia's table of results.
The alliance of the 2025 winner, written NDA, INDIA or Other.
The 2025 winning margin in votes, the winner's votes less the runner-up's, from the Election Commission's 2025 results.
Votes polled at the 2025 election, worked out as the published turnout percentage times electorate_2025 and rounded to a whole number.
Electors on the draft roll of 1 August 2025, from the Election Commission's Format 4B return for Bihar's final roll.
Names added between the draft roll and the final roll of 30 September 2025 (claims admitted), as a count from Format 4B.
Names deleted between the draft roll and the final roll of 30 September 2025 (objections admitted), as a count from Format 4B.
Electors on the final roll of 30 September 2025, from Format 4B.
The final roll less the draft roll, a net change that counts new voters added after the draft as well as any names put back.
Phase 1 names left off the draft less final_less_draft, which is the net fall in the roll from before the revision to the final roll, as a count.

sheets.what: Every Bihar district, with names left off or deleted, the reasons, women's share and the range for Muslim names
columns: The district's name as the Bihar constituency table spells it.
The number of assembly constituencies in the district.
Names left off or deleted in both phases, summed over the district's constituencies from the Chief Electoral Officer's table of what it calls deletions by constituency.
Names left off or deleted in both phases per 100 electors, with the constituencies' 2025 electorate from Wikipedia's list as the base.
The border the district lies on (Nepal, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand or West Bengal, with two joined by a semicolon character) or Interior where it lies on none.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as dead, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off, where the reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as shifted, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as absent, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off.
Phase 1 names left off the draft entered as already enrolled somewhere else, counted from the row-level phase 1 lists of names left off.
